open_points.subject: Randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns the random source, identifier representation and collision-retry mechanism used by all five record-writing modules?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks every random identity atomically
Each domain module mints its own identities under one explicitly shared algorithm
A new lower-level identity module owns random minting and collision retry
open_points.default_guess: Make `store` mint and collision-check the identities inside the record-creation transaction.

open_points.subject: Shared port-declaration validation
open_points.text: The list runs from the bottom of the stack up: a module may know only modules on earlier lines of the list, never one on a later line, and modules on one line do not know each other. ... `functions` Owns A02 ... `bindings` ... refuses when its ports break a rule A02 sets for contract ports.
open_points.question: Who owns the common validation of port names, carriage/media-type consistency and disclosure-class placement, and how may peer module `bindings` use rules currently owned by `functions`?
options: Move the common port-declaration validator to `canonical_values`
Give `functions` and `bindings` separate explicitly authoritative validators
Move the shared rules to another lower-level module
open_points.default_guess: Put the common port-declaration validation in `canonical_values`, with `functions` and `bindings` owning only their context-specific checks.

open_points.subject: Captured execution provenance
open_points.text: `runs` passes to `functions.add_captured_trial_case` the pinned contract version and the inputs of the record it captures ... `functions` checks that the record's pinned contract version is the one named.
open_points.question: How can `functions` verify the captured record's contract-version provenance when the stated call passes the claimed contract version and inputs, but not the NodeExecution or its executed implementation identity?
options: `runs` owns the provenance check and `functions` trusts the checked contract version
Pass the NodeExecution or executed implementation identity so `functions` verifies provenance
Have `store` validate the association atomically while adding the case
open_points.default_guess: Let `runs` verify provenance through `functions.read_implementation`, then let `functions` validate only the resulting case against the named contract.

open_points.subject: HTTP header-name and value validation
open_points.text: The installation's configuration file holds ... a header name — an HTTP field-name token, or the kernel refuses to start ... [a manifest instance is refused when it] has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`.
open_points.question: Which lower module owns the exact HTTP field-name-token and header-value validation used independently by `installation`, `bindings` and `service_invoker`?
options: Separate validators in all three modules with an explicit conformance rule
open_points.default_guess: Use one shared lower-level validator exposed by `canonical_values` and consumed by all three modules.
